subject: Latency-constrained pilot: credits vs commit and quantization trade-offs
messages:
From: Sofia Patel <sofia.patel@finmetrics.io>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot idea + ask on credits vs commit + quantization guidance

Hi Rishi,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency and cost numbers looked promising. Were trying to stand up a small pilot (3 months) to validate inference economics on our vector similarity + short-generation workloads. A few details from our side:

- Expected peak: ~18 qps, steady-state ~6 qps.
- Avg prompt+response token length: ~420 tokens.
- Primary goal: P95 end-to-end <= 250ms for our web UI.

Procurement asked for two pricing options for internal review:
1) A credits-based pilot (no commit) with a way for us to turn caching on/off and see the delta.
2) A short committed band (3 months) with a pilot discount and extra credits applied if we enable KV cache.

Wed also like a quick technical note on quantization: for our mix of re-ranking and short generations, which quantization approach do you recommend (int8 / q4 / other) and what quality loss you've observed in similar workloads?

Attached is a short requirements doc for procurement (pilot_requirements.pdf). Can you send an initial sketch of pricing and a recommended model/config so we can align with our infra team?

Best,
Sofia
Sofia Patel
Head of Platform 
FinMetrics

--
Attachment: pilot_requirements.pdf (2 pages)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Patel <sofia.patel@finmetrics.io>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot idea + ask on credits vs commit + quantization guidance

Hi Sofia — thanks for the clear write-up and the numbers. Quick responses below and an initial pricing sketch attached.

Short answer on structure:
- Credits pilot: flexible, no minimum; we can enable KV cache for the pilot and meter cache hits separately. Good if youre unsure of volume.
- Short commit (3m): we recommend a small reserved band sized to your expected steady-state (e.g., 50k tokens/min) + burst capacity. Committed bands get volume discounts and priority routing for latency-sensitive SLOs.

Quantization guidance (high level):
- Recommended starting point: 8-bit symmetric quantization (INT8) for GPUs where weve validated the model. In our benchmarks for similar generation/re-rank mixes, INT8 delivered ~1.9–2.3x token throughput vs fp16 with typical quality delta <2% on BLEU/ROUGE-type metrics for short gen. Re-ranking tasks saw even smaller deltas (often <1%).
- If youre extremely sensitive to worst-case quality on open-ended generation, we can run an eval set and recommend a per-prompt fallback to fp16 for flagged prompts.

Latency and caching:
- KV cache on reads cut per-request soft latency by ~30–45% on workloads with repeated prefixes; cold starts still governed by base model latency.
- For a P95 <= 250ms target I want to confirm: do you mean application-level E2E (including network) or our inference-only p95? If E2E, well need to size for <180ms inference p95 to leave headroom.

Attached: pilot_pricing_sketch.xlsx (two scenarios: credits vs commit). Numbers are placeholders but show tradeoffs.

Next step: can we do a technical sync Monday or Tuesday? Ill loop Lauren for commercial sizing.

Thanks,
Rishi
Director, Solutions
Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: pilot_pricing_sketch.xlsx (spreadsheet with two scenarios)

Thanks Rishi and Lauren — this is helpful. A few clarifications from procurement and engineering:

- Our procurement team wants a pricing table that shows: cache OFF (baseline), cache ON (expected hit rate 40–60%), and a line for quantized (INT8) vs non-quantized. Put those side-by-side if possible.
- For latency: our SREs will want E2E P95 <= 250ms. Can you confirm the inference-only P95 target we should expect for the commit band?
- Quantization: re-ranking is critical (high precision). If INT8 shows a 1–2% delta on our evals, that may be acceptable; for open-ended generation wed prefer fallbacks. Please include a short note on how you run per-prompt fallbacks.

Procurement also prefers an option with a short PO (3 months) so they can start payments while we evaluate. I attached our procurement checklist (procurement_requirements.docx).

Could you also share the benchmark CSV you mentioned in the sketch? Wed like to feed it to our performance team.

Best,
Sofia

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Patel <sofia.patel@finmetrics.io>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot idea + ask on credits vs commit + quantization guidance

Sofia — thanks, and really appreciate the procurement checklist. Attaching the benchmark CSV and a more explicit pricing table (pilot_pricing_final.xlsx + benchmark_results.csv). Summary below so procurement can paste into the PO:

Pricing scenarios (summary):
1) Credits-only pilot (no commit)
   - Baseline (cache OFF, fp16): $0.018 per 1k tokens
   - Cache ON (expected 50% hit): effective cost ~ $0.012 per 1k tokens (measured from cache hit delta)
   - INT8 quantized path: additional perf benefit; we estimate throughput uplift of ~2.0x and cost multiplier improvement to ~$0.007–0.010 effective per 1k tokens if you run quantized end-to-end (depends on hit rate).

2) 3-month short commit (recommended)
   - Commit tier sized at ~60% steady: list price equivalent $0.015 per 1k tokens
   - Pilot discount: 20% off list for the committed band (net $0.012 per 1k tokens)
   - KV-cache incentive: +25% bonus credits on top of monthly committed allocation when cache-hit thresholds are met (e.g., 40%+ hit rate).
   - Well include a pilot SLA addendum that guarantees inference-only P95 <= 180ms for requests routed to the committed band (this leaves ~70ms for network + app to meet your E2E 250ms target). If we cant meet that, well add prioritized capacity until targets are met.

Technical notes:
- Quantization fallback: we propose an eval-based gating + per-request quality signal that routes flagged prompts to fp16. Aditya will own the eval run for your sample set and share a per-prompt pass/fail matrix.
- Benchmarks: attached benchmark_results.csv shows fp16 vs INT8 vs cache-on numbers for similar payloads.

Next steps:
- Ill upload the finalized pricing sheet to HubSpot and attach the PO-friendly summary. Link: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/12345/FM-4921
- Aditya: can you run the eval on Sofias sample prompts and return recommendations by EOD Wednesday?
- Procurement: if the PO is ready we can consume it and spin up the committed band within 48 hours of receiving signed PO.

Thanks — looping Lauren and Connor for commercial and ops follow-up.

Rishi
Director, Solutions
Redwood Inference
